# AudioLoader { #timetoalign.loader.AudioLoader }

```python
loader.AudioLoader()
```

Load audio file metadata for creating physical timelines.

AudioLoader extracts metadata from audio files without loading the actual
sample data. This is efficient for creating seconds-based physical
timelines that represent audio files in the TimeToAlign! framework.

The loader automatically:
- Detects the best available backend (soundfile > mutagen > wave)
- Extracts sample count, sample rate, channels, and format info
- Provides a timeline constructor over a continuous seconds axis

Supported formats depend on installed backends:
- soundfile: WAV, FLAC, OGG, AIFF, and many more (via libsndfile)
- mutagen: MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG (metadata only, may not have exact sample count)
- wave (builtin): WAV only

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> loader = AudioLoader()
>>> loader.load("recording.wav")
>>> loader.n_samples
7938048
>>> loader.sample_rate
44100
>>> loader.duration_seconds
180.0
```

```python
>>> # Create a timeline
>>> timeline = loader.create_timeline(uid="my_audio")
>>> timeline.unit
<TimeUnit.seconds: 'seconds'>
>>> timeline.length
Coordinate(180.0, seconds)
```

### create_samples_to_seconds_map { #timetoalign.loader.AudioLoader.create_samples_to_seconds_map }

```python
loader.AudioLoader.create_samples_to_seconds_map()
```

Create a SamplesToSeconds conversion map for this audio.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                 | Description                                                        |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'SamplesToSeconds\' | A SamplesToSeconds C-map configured with this audio's sample rate. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                       |
|--------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
|        | [RuntimeError](`RuntimeError`) | If no audio file has been loaded. |

### create_timeline { #timetoalign.loader.AudioLoader.create_timeline }

```python
loader.AudioLoader.create_timeline(uid=None, name=None, attach_cmap=True)
```

Create a continuous seconds timeline from the loaded audio.

The timeline is created with:
- unit=TimeUnit.seconds
- length=duration_seconds
- float coordinates

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                 | Description                                                                               | Default   |
|-------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| uid         | [str](`str`) \| None | Unique identifier for the timeline. If None, uses filename.                               | `None`    |
| name        | [str](`str`) \| None | Human-readable name. If None, uses filename.                                              | `None`    |
| attach_cmap | [bool](`bool`)       | Accepted for loader-call compatibility; seconds need no sample-to-seconds conversion map. | `True`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                                 |
|--------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'ContinuousPhysicalTimeline\' | A continuous physical timeline representing the audio file. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                       |
|--------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
|        | [RuntimeError](`RuntimeError`) | If no audio file has been loaded. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> loader = AudioLoader().load("song.wav")
>>> timeline = loader.create_timeline()
>>> timeline.unit
<TimeUnit.seconds: 'seconds'>
```

### from_file { #timetoalign.loader.AudioLoader.from_file }

```python
loader.AudioLoader.from_file(path)
```

Load an audio file and return the loader (convenience constructor).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                   | Description             | Default    |
|--------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------|------------|
| path   | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| [str](`str`) | Path to the audio file. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type            | Description                                  |
|--------|-----------------|----------------------------------------------|
|        | \'AudioLoader\' | An AudioLoader with the file already loaded. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> loader = AudioLoader.from_file("song.wav")
>>> print(loader.duration_seconds)
```
